summary: The milestone completed 12 experiments in 111.8 minutes. The two longest synthesis-only entries consumed 107.12 minutes, about 96% of the wall time, while the longest listed compute-bound experiment, Three-family delayed syntax-tail A/B, took 1.17 minutes. No data available this milestone explains that compute duration at phase level.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis throughput dominated elapsed time: Independent constraint-family prequential stream took 57.4 minutes and V582 five-branch disposition took 49.72 minutes, jointly consuming 107.12 of 111.8 minutes.
The disk-mtime fallback provides experiment-level durations but no phase or wait-state attribution, so the cause of the 1.17-minute compute leader cannot be determined.
No data available this milestone identifies a task that loaded 2 or more models in parallel, so DualGPURunner applicability and dispatch compliance cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Add dependency-aware concurrent scheduling for independent synthesis-only workflows, with bounded workers and deterministic artifact reconciliation.
Emit monotonic per-experiment phase receipts for queue, setup, synthesis, verification, and artifact-write time, plus straggler alerts for long synthesis phases.
Record task-window GPU utilization, model count, and runner selection; choose DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Overlap dependency-independent synthesis-only workflows; perfect overlap of the two longest entries has a 49.72-minute theoretical ceiling.
Replace disk-mtime-only diagnosis with monotonic phase and wait-state receipts so the next long synthesis phase has an attributable cause.
Add model-count and runner-selection receipts alongside task-scoped GPU telemetry, without enforcing DualGPURunner for single-model work.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports a synthesis scheduling and observability priority, not a GPU-idle diagnosis: gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false, and the final idle snapshot is not task-window evidence. The 44% estimate is a theoretical ceiling derived from 49.72 divided by 111.8, rounded to an integer, and applies only if the two longest synthesis workflows are dependency-independent and can overlap fully.
